pr_title: ensure that sync Connect calls ShouldRetrySyncOperation
pr_body:
I believe this is the root of the issue in #50380.

Other sync socket calls (send, recv, etc) call ShouldRetrySyncOperation in order to distinguish between a timeout on a sync socket vs EAGAIN on a socket that's been forced into nonblocking mode. The Connect operation isn't, which means that we are misinterpreting some timeouts as meaning that the socket is now nonblocking.

Fixes #50380

That's the same assert I saw on my PR here: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/48758

From the stacktrace, it looks like the `_nonBlockingSet` of `SocketAsyncContext` for which the assert fails, and `_nonBlocking` which is used at `SocketPal.Connect` to start using `SocketAsyncContext` are out-of-sync.

This relates to @benaadams' PR  https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/37573.

cc @antonfirsov @scalablecory

> This relates to @benaadams' PR #37573.

Yeah it does maintain two fields for the same thing which don't necessarily agree or correctly reflect the state; should probably only be one field; but I ran out of time trying to fix it and it didn't seem too important 😅

The two flags do different things.

_nonBlocking on the SafeHandle indicates that the user has requested a non-blocking Socket. This will always force the OS socket to be non-blocking.

_nonBlockingSet on SocketAsyncContext indicates whether the OS handle has been set to non-blocking. This happens either because the user explicitly requested it, or because the user did an asynchronous operation.

I have trouble understanding this
`TryStartXXX || !ShouldRetrySyncOperation(out errorCode)` pattern.

The `TryStart` method returns `false` when `EAGAIN`. `EAGAIN` can only happen when the socket is non-blocking. When `_nonBlockingSet` is `true`, `ShouldRetrySyncOperation` returns `true`.

`false || !true` is still `false`.

See here: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/src/libraries/System.Net.Sockets/src/System/Net/Sockets/SocketAsyncContext.Unix.cs#L1398

Apparently we get EAGAIN for timeouts on blocking sockets.

I merged this fix into my request retry PR, which was consistently seeing the SocketAsyncContext assert, and the assert doesn't seem to repro anymore. That seems like pretty good evidence that this fix is correct.

Thoughts?

Ah, yes, for timeouts it can happen as well.

From man 7 socket:

> if  no  data  has been  transferred  and  the timeout has been reached, then -1 is returned with errno set to EAGAIN or EWOULDBLOCK, or EINPROGRESS (for connect(2)) just as if the socket was specified to  be  nonblocking
